flawed_pattern: Including human speech, dialogue, or spoken battle cries inside MiniMax H3's overall_soundscape.
prevention_rule: The overall_soundscape must contain exclusively diegetic foley and environment audio (wind, boot crunch, armor rattle, conch blares). It MUST strictly state: 'Strict rule: absolutely no human speech or dialogue.' Human dialogue causes grotesque video mouth-morphing artifacts.
example_bad: overall_soundscape: War conch blares, soldiers shouting 'Charge!', distant screams.
example_good: overall_soundscape: War conch blares, heavy boot thuds on gravel, cold wind howl through bronze armor. Strict rule: absolutely no human speech or dialogue.

flawed_pattern: Using abstract emotional labels ('felt sad', 'was terrified', 'became furious') instead of physical somatic sensations.
prevention_rule: Never state the emotion as an adjective; evoke the emotion through autonomic body responses (cold sweat, trembling grip on bow, hollow ache in throat, breath catching).
example_bad: Arjuna was deeply saddened as he looked at Bhishma.
example_good: A hot, suffocating knot tightened in Arjuna's throat as his fingers slipped against the taut silk of the Gandiva.

flawed_pattern: Changing established character appearance, eye color, scars, or armor materials across scenes.
prevention_rule: Every character's established visual tags must be preserved verbatim in all subsequent descriptions and prompts without hallucinating changes.
example_bad: Scene 1: Bhishma in weathered golden breastplate. Scene 2: Bhishma in black iron tunic.
example_good: All scenes: Bhishma in weathered golden breastplate with sun crest, white beard with gold ash.

flawed_pattern: Using the same camera movement or framing vector in 2 or more consecutive shots (e.g. push-in after push-in).
prevention_rule: Always alternate shot types and camera vectors: Wide Establishing ➔ Medium Tracking ➔ Macro Close-Up; push-in ➔ lateral track ➔ low-angle tilt.
example_bad: Shot 1: Slow push-in. Shot 2: Steadicam push-in. Shot 3: Slow push-in.
example_good: Shot 1: Wide panoramic low-angle crane. Shot 2: Ground-level lateral tracking shot. Shot 3: Macro close-up static push-in.

flawed_pattern: Using proper names directly in text-to-image prompts without visual descriptor tags.
prevention_rule: In Qwen Image 2.1 prompts, unname the character into visual tags: 'venerable silver-haired warrior in weathered golden breastplate', not bare proper names that the art model cannot interpret.
example_bad: Masterpiece photo of Arjuna in Kurukshetra.
example_good: Masterpiece photo, youthful muscular dark-skinned warrior with crimson archer sash, silver-embossed armguards, taut celestial bow.

flawed_pattern: Blindly injecting protagonist anchor image and character description into every panel prompt, causing the protagonist to appear in every single frame in the exact same static chained-wrist pose while only the background changes.
prevention_rule: Only condition on protagonist anchor when the protagonist is the explicit subject. For environmental vistas, props, macro shots, or secondary characters, generate the specific subject directly. When protagonist is present, explicitly choreograph varied combat poses, angles, and facial expressions—never repeat the anchor pose.
example_bad: Panel 1 (Wide quarry abyss) Prompt: [CHARACTER: Chen Ye ... shattered iron cuffs] wide basalt quarry in rain.
example_good: Panel 1 (Wide quarry abyss) Prompt: wide panoramic vista of massive basalt quarry, rain slicked stone, violet eclipse halo in sky, no people.

flawed_pattern: Generating generic character frames that fail to visually illustrate the specific event described in the narration line.
prevention_rule: Every panel must be a direct visual translation of its narration line. If the narration describes a weapon shattering, the image must be a macro shot of shattering steel. If narration introduces an antagonist, the image must depict that antagonist.
example_bad: Narration describes ancient altar breaking; Image shows Chen Ye looking at his hands.
example_good: Narration describes ancient altar breaking; Image shows the ancient obsidian altar cracking open with divine violet light.

flawed_pattern: Using raw FFmpeg zoompan formulas with low-resolution integer coordinates, producing an unwatchable sub-pixel shaky/jittery camera effect.
prevention_rule: Never use unpadded low-res zoompan. Pre-scale to high resolution (3840x2160) before zoompan or use smooth float-precision pans and cinematic static holds with gentle motion to ensure rock-solid, jitter-free camera dynamics.

flawed_pattern: Reciting narration at flat, monotone default rates without expressive storytelling cadence, breath pauses, or emotional modulation.
prevention_rule: Apply expressive storytelling parameters: slight pacing reduction (-4% to -6%) for gravitas, natural punctuation pauses, and dynamic dramatic cadence matching the emotional beat of the scene.
example_bad: Flat, high-speed default TTS delivery sounding synthetic and robotic.
example_good: Grounded, resonant storyteller cadence with deliberate pauses between narrative clauses.

flawed_pattern: Generating background environments ad-hoc per panel without locked geographic landmarks, causing sudden, jarring shifts (e.g. from mountain cliff to crowd to inside caves with completely different geology/lighting) while the story is still in the same location.
prevention_rule: Maintain a strict Scene Environment State. Lock persistent landmarks (e.g. Abyssal Basalt Quarry: massive black hexagonal basalt walls, violet crystal veins, rain-slick stone floor, dark stormy sky with purple aurora). Retain these exact environmental tokens across all shots in that scene. If the camera angle changes (wide, over-the-shoulder, close-up), the background elements must reflect the same environment from that specific perspective.
example_bad: Shot 1 shows mountain cliff edge. Shot 2 suddenly shows him in a crowded bustling marketplace. Shot 3 shows an underground limestone cavern.
example_good: Shot 1 (Wide): Rain-slicked black basalt quarry with violet crystal veins. Shot 2 (Medium): Antagonist standing against the same black basalt quarry wall. Shot 3 (Close-Up): Chen Ye with the same violet crystal vein glowing in background blur.

flawed_pattern: Allowing secondary characters, enforcers, soldiers, or side characters to change armor design, helmet style, face, or weapons from shot to shot.
prevention_rule: Maintain locked Faction and Character Visual Specifications. Every recurring secondary character or faction squad must have standardized, immutable prompt tokens (e.g. Lingxiao Iron Enforcer: identical matte-black spiked segmented plate armor, crimson glowing visor slit on closed iron helm, wielding double-edged serrated black steel halberds) and condition on a dedicated anchor image when featured.
example_bad: Soldier in Shot 1 has shiny silver European plate armor with open visor. Soldier in Shot 2 has black spiked armor with a full face mask. Soldier in Shot 3 has leather tunic.
example_good: All soldiers in all shots wear identical matte-black spiked segmented plate armor with narrow crimson visor slits and wield double-edged serrated black steel halberds.

flawed_pattern: Using awkward, disorienting camera angles, disjointed framing, or flipping the 180-degree spatial action axis between cuts.
prevention_rule: Direct scenes using professional cinematic coverage: Establishing Wide Shot (EWS) -> Full/Medium Shot (FS/MS) -> Over-the-Shoulder (OTS) -> Close-Up (CU) -> Dynamic Action / Dutch Angle -> Resolution. Preserve screen direction: protagonist faces screen-right; antagonists face screen-left; camera remains on one side of the action vector.
example_bad: Awkward unmotivated extreme high-angle tilted ceiling shot, followed by an eye-line flip where characters swap screen sides.
example_good: Establishing Wide Shot showing spatial geography, followed by OTS framing Chen Ye looking at the Enforcer on screen-left, cut to MCU of Chen Ye amethyst eyes.

flawed_pattern: Fragmenting narration into isolated audio clips with arbitrary dead silence gaps between cuts, or reciting the entire story at a flat speed without emotional modulation, breaking listener immersion.
prevention_rule: Synthesize a continuous, fluid master storyteller performance using nuanced prosody and emotional cadence. Dramatic pauses must occur ONLY where story tension demands it (e.g. before an explosive blow or revelation). Voice speed, pitch, and energy must dynamically modulate: hushed reverence for ancient mysteries, rising urgency for martial clashes, and measured gravitas for narration.
example_bad: Robotic narration interrupted by 1-second awkward silence gaps at every panel cut.
example_good: Continuous human-like storytelling cadence flowing seamlessly across cuts with dramatic suspense pauses placed deliberately at emotional peaks.

flawed_pattern: Flipping spatial screen direction in action clash shots (having protagonist punch toward screen-left when the established axis is left-to-right) or dropping helmet assets on enemy soldiers (generating them bare-headed or without full-face barbute helm).
prevention_rule: Always enforce directional screen orientation (Chen Ye on screen-left attacking screen-right; Enforcer on screen-right facing screen-left). For faction soldiers, inject strict negative prompts (bare head on soldier, human hair on soldier, open face on soldier, skin face on soldier) and bind both protagonist and faction reference images simultaneously.
example_bad: Panel 12: Chen Ye on center-right punching left; soldier on far left with bare head and visible ear/neck.
example_good: Panel 12: Chen Ye on screen-left lunging right; soldier on screen-right wearing full matte-black iron barbute helm with horizontal crimson slit visor.

flawed_pattern: Switching opponent identity midway through a multi-shot combat sequence (e.g. establishing Commander Meng as the boss in Shot 7 and having Commander Meng crash into the wall in Shot 13, but rendering a generic helmeted soldier taking the punch in Shot 12).
prevention_rule: In sequential combat beats, the entity who attacks, the entity who receives the strike, and the entity who suffers the aftermath in the following frame must be the exact same character with identical armor, face, and reference anchor.
example_bad: Shot 12 shows a helmeted generic enforcer being punched; Shot 13 shows unhelmeted Commander Meng with topknot and dragon pauldron crashing into the wall.
example_good: Shot 12 shows Commander Meng (topknot, scarred jaw, dragon pauldron) being punched in the chestplate; Shot 13 shows Commander Meng smashing into the basalt wall.

flawed_pattern: Showing a character holding an intact weapon in an aftermath frame when that weapon was explicitly shattered or lost in an earlier frame.
prevention_rule: When a weapon is shattered or lost, all subsequent shots in that scene must set weapon_in_hand=None, enforce empty hands in the positive prompt, and inject strict negative prompts banning that weapon (e.g. 'sword, blade, cleaver, weapon in hand, holding weapon').
example_bad: Shot 11: Broadsword shatters into shards. Shot 13: Commander Meng stands against the wall holding an intact broadsword.
example_good: Shot 11: Broadsword shatters into shards. Shot 12: Commander Meng struck with empty hands. Shot 13: Commander Meng slumped in crater with empty hands bracing against shattered stone.

flawed_pattern: Depicting an opponent with pristine, unblemished armor and casual posture in an aftermath shot immediately following a strike that crushed their breastplate.
prevention_rule: Aftermath shots must physically reflect the damage from the preceding hit: cracked/caved inward armor, residual energy smoke/sparks, reeling or slumped posture in the crater, and negative prompts banning pristine armor ('clean undamaged armor, smooth chestplate, standing upright').
example_bad: Shot 12: Void fist crushes Meng's chestplate with purple shockwave. Shot 13: Meng has polished smooth armor and stands calmly.
example_good: Shot 12: Void fist crushes Meng's chestplate. Shot 13: Meng embedded in wall crater, breastplate caved inward with violet void smoke and purple sparks crackling on the fractured iron.
